name: prenatal genetic screening overview
title: Prenatal genetic screening: before pregnancy take the family history and offer carrier screening by ancestry; in pregnancy a screen (NT and eFTS, MSS, the anatomy scan's soft markers, NIPT) gives a risk and a positive screen leads to NIPT or a diagnostic test, while CVS and amniocentesis give a definitive diagnosis at a small miscarriage risk

root.title: Prenatal genetics: a SCREEN gives a RISK · a DIAGNOSTIC test gives the ANSWER
lines: BEFORE pregnancy: 3-generation pedigree, red flags → refer · carrier screening by ancestry: the MOTHER first, the partner if she is a carrier
IN pregnancy: offer every couple screening after discussion; they opt in or out · baseline 2–3% congenital anomaly whatever the screen

groups.title: SCREEN: non-invasive, gives a RISK
lines: screen POSITIVE → NIPT, or straight to a diagnostic test

head: h
Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT)
cell-free fetal DNA in maternal blood
det: previous trisomy · age 40+ · NT > 3.5 · positive eFTS
~Ontario: NOT first line for low risk
next: still a SCREEN → CONFIRM by CVS or amnio
risk: the DNA is mainly PLACENTAL: a screen, not a diagnosis

head: h
NT ultrasound + eFTS
nuchal translucency + 1st-trimester serum markers
det: trisomy 13, 18, 45,X · heart defect · Noonan, skeletal dysplasia

head: h
Maternal serum screen (MSS)
triple or quad serum markers
needs NO ultrasound
det: for a woman too late for eFTS, or with no NT ultrasound
gestational age · ultrasound access · early result vs detection

head: h
Anatomy scan
detailed fetal ultrasound
det: choroid plexus cyst · short femur · echogenic heart focus · echogenic bowel
next: matters only with ABNORMAL serum markers
risk: NEVER ASSUME what the couple wants: offer all options

head: h
Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)
the earliest diagnosis
det: single gene: down to 1 bp, ~3 weeks
next: offer ALL options, never judge: continue · terminate (< 24 wk) · plan delivery
risk: maternal cell contamination · confined placental mosaicism

head: h
Amniocentesis
the later diagnosis
det: Amniotic fluid, needle through the abdomen
fetal cells for chromosomes or genes
next: offer ALL options, never judge: continue · terminate (< 24 wk) · plan delivery

panels.title: Before pregnancy: carrier screening by ancestry
items: EUROPEAN: cystic fibrosis (recurrent mutation analysis) · carriers 1 in 24
Middle Eastern, South Asian, or MCV < 80 fL: thalassemia + hemoglobinopathies
ASHKENAZI JEWISH: panel incl. Tay-Sachs, Canavan, familial dysautonomia
FRENCH-CANADIAN (Bas-St-Laurent, Gaspésie, New Brunswick): Tay-Sachs, 1 in 14
Amish + Old Order Mennonite: their community's panel
test the MOTHER first → the partner only if she is a carrier

panels.title: Before pregnancy: red flags → refer to genetics
items: male infertility from absent vas deferens (cystic fibrosis)
fragile X: ovarian insufficiency < 40 · male relatives with ataxia + tremor
folic acid 0.8–1 mg from 3 months before conception

panels.title: A positive screen: what next
items: eFTS / MSS / NT > 3.5 positive → NIPT (a better SCREEN) or straight to CVS / amnio
NIPT positive → CONFIRM with CVS (11–13 wk) or amnio (15–20 wk)
ask: do they want to know DEFINITIVELY, and will it change management?
